t3.descripcion:
To talk about media and press, you need to master these terms:
• Print press: periódico, revista, diario, semanario, suplemento.
• Audiovisual media: telediario, informativo, noticias, reportaje, documental.
• Radio: emisora, programación, oyente, locutor.
• Digital media: periódico digital, blog, red social, portal de noticias.
• Professionals: periodista, reportero, corresponsal, editor, presentador.
• Actions: publicar, difundir, informar, entrevistar, retransmitir.
📌 IMPORTANT NOTE: «Diario» and «periódico» are synonyms in Spain, but in Latin America «diario» is used less; «noticias» in plural designates the set of information.
❌ COMMON ERROR: Chinese speakers often say «mirar las noticias» when the correct form is «ver las noticias» or «leer las noticias» depending on the medium.
ejemplos: Leo el periódico todas las mañanas para informarme.
El telediario de las nueve es el más visto en España.
La emisora de radio emite noticias cada hora.
El periódico digital actualiza las noticias constantemente.
El corresponsal en Bruselas informó sobre la cumbre europea.

t2.titulo: Structure of a news article: headline, lead and body
t2.descripcion:
The news article is organised into three fundamental parts:
• The headline: a brief and striking phrase that summarises the most important information. It usually omits articles and copulative verbs.
• The lead (or entradilla): the first paragraph that expands on the headline and answers the 5W (what, who, when, where, why).
• The body: development of the information in decreasing order of importance (inverted pyramid).
• Typographic resources: bold, italics, quotation marks for direct quotes.
• The closing: sometimes includes contextual information or final statements.
📌 IMPORTANT NOTE: The headline must be clear and attractive, but never misleading; the lead must be able to be read independently.
❌ COMMON ERROR: Chinese students tend to write headlines that are too long and with conjugated verbs; in journalistic Spanish, nominal constructions or infinitives are preferred.
ejemplos: Titular: «Gobierno anuncia nuevas medidas económicas».
Entradilla: «El presidente compareció ayer en rueda de prensa para detallar el plan».
Cuerpo: «Las medidas incluyen reducciones fiscales y ayudas directas a familias».
El titular usa comillas para citar las palabras exactas del ministro.
La entradilla responde a las preguntas básicas del periodismo.

t4.descripcion:
Journalistic language seeks clarity, concision, and objectivity, but uses stylistic resources:
• Short sentences and brief paragraphs to facilitate reading.
• Use of the third person and direct style (quotation marks) to cite sources.
• Verbs in the present to update facts, and preterite for background.
• Evaluative adjectives in opinion genres, but not in the news story.
• Acronyms and initialisms (ONU, UE, OTAN) that must be explained the first time.
📌 IMPORTANT NOTE: Objectivity does not mean absolute neutrality; the journalist selects facts, but must contrast sources.
❌ COMMON ERROR: Chinese students sometimes overuse the passive reflexive voice («se informa que»), when in journalistic Spanish active constructions with a clear subject are preferred.
ejemplos: El ministro declaró: «Vamos a invertir más en educación».
Según fuentes policiales, el accidente se produjo por exceso de velocidad.
La OTAN (Organización del Tratado del Atlántico Norte) se reúne hoy.
El periodista evitó adjetivos valorativos en la noticia.
El reportaje combina datos objetivos con testimonios personales.

t1.titulo: Journalistic genres: the news and the feature
t1.descripcion:
In written journalism, the main informative genres are the news and the feature.
• La noticia: a brief and objective text that answers the key questions (what, who, when, where, how, why).
• El reportaje: a longer and more in-depth text that combines information with analysis, testimonies and context.
• La entrevista: a dialogue between a journalist and a relevant person.
• La crónica: a chronological narration of an event with interpretive value.
• El editorial: an opinion article that reflects the ideological line of the media outlet.
📌 IMPORTANT NOTE: La noticia must be objective and truthful; el reportaje may include more interpretation, but always based on facts.
❌ COMMON MISTAKE: Chinese speakers often confuse «noticia» with «artículo»; in Spanish, «noticia» is the information about a recent event, while «artículo» is an opinion or informative text.
ejemplos: La noticia del terremoto apareció en la portada de todos los periódicos.
El reportaje sobre el cambio climático incluye entrevistas a científicos.
La entrevista al presidente se publicó en la revista del domingo.
La crónica del partido destacó la actuación del portero.
El editorial criticó duramente la nueva ley de educación.

dict.数字时代纸质报刊的转型: The transformation of print media in the digital age
dict.在过去的几十年里，由于互联网和移动设备的冲击，纸质报刊经历了深刻的变革。许多传统: In recent decades, due to the impact of the internet and mobile devices, print media has undergone profound changes. Many traditional newspapers that used to appear at newsstands every morning now face a declining print readership. To adapt, they have created digital versions and diversified content through supplements, opinion columns, and multimedia reports.
dict.然而，这一变化并非易事。记者们必须更快地工作，并处理多种信息来源，这有时会危及对: However, this change is not easy. Journalists must work faster and handle multiple sources of information, which sometimes jeopardizes fact-checking. Moreover, competition with social media and online news outlets forces newspapers to find new ways to attract audiences. Some experts point out that the key is to provide high-quality journalism, with well-argued editorials and a clear distinction between news and opinion.

Therefore, adapting to the digital environment is an unavoidable challenge, but also an opportunity to reinvent the profession.
